title: Human-in-the-Loop Canary Escalation Decision Trees (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects working notes and compact decision trees for cases where a human-in-the-loop (HITL) must evaluate/hold/revert a canary or AB slice. Goal: reduce cognitive load for oncall/stewards and standardize escalation thresholds across product, SRE, and trust/safety.

Audience:
- Oncall operatives (stewards) running microcanaries
- Product leads running AB experiments with LLM changes
- SRE/observability engineers who maintain signals
- Trust & Safety reviewers for behavioral regressions

Scope & assumptions:
- Covers user-visible canaries (frontend features, rerankers, assistant responses) and backend model swaps where human review is a required gate before broad exposure.
- Assumes telemetry (latency, error-rate, quality delta, safety flags, human review queue length) is available in console dashboards and can trigger Slack pagers.
- Not a full runbook; this is decision-tree focused guidance + alert templates and example walk-throughs.

Top-level decision trees (summary):
1) Safety-first failure (to trust/safety)
  - Trigger: safety-alert-rate > 0.01% over baseline OR 3+ distinct high-severity flags in 30m
  - Immediate action: PAUSE canary traffic (auto fallback to baseline). Notify trust-safety via #trust-safety-escalations and page product-oncall.
  - Human step: Triage sample set (20 flagged examples) -> classify as false positive / threshold tuning / model regression.
  - Outcomes: 
    * false positive -> adjust detector or exclusion slice, resume at 10% with monitoring cadence 
    * regression -> rollback and open Jira with triage notes + CI reproducible sample set

2) Latency/cost breach (infrastructure)
  - Trigger: p95 latency > SLO + 30% sustained for 10m OR sudden token cost per request increase > 2x baseline
  - Immediate action: scale up dedicated pool OR temporarily throttle canary traffic to micro-slice (2-5%).
  - Human step: SRE validates kernel selection/quantization variant, checks autoscale logs. If not resolvable within 30m, fallback to cheaper model variant.

3) Quality drift (user experience)
  - Trigger: primary user-metric (CTR, acceptance, rerank NDCG) delta beyond pre-committed guardrail (e.g., > -3% absolute) AND automated evals show drop on seed prompt set
  - Decision tree: 
    * Is the delta concentrated in a cohort (locale, device)? -> If yes, quarantine cohort, keep other cohorts running.
    * If global, take an immediate 20% traffic pause and run human review on 100 randomized responses.
    * If majority (>60%) of human reviewers mark responses as degraded -> rollback.

4) Ambiguous/weak signal (require human judgement)
  - Trigger: conflicting signals (latency ok, safety ok, small quality dip but automated evals inconclusive)
  - Action: elevate to steward for curated A/B interpretive review (10–20 min session). If steward time unavailable, escalate to product owner.

Compact decision trees (ASCII):

[SIGNAL] -> classify -> [safety?] -> yes -> pause + page T&S -> human triage -> rollback/adjust/resume
          -> [infra?] -> yes -> throttle/scale -> SRE triage -> variant fallback / resume
          -> [quality?] -> yes -> cohort quarantine -> human review -> rollback/resume

Checklist for steward when a page arrives:
- Pull the top 100 recent requests for the canary slice (console -> sample explorer).
- Run quick safety triage: scan for obvious hallucinations, disallowed content, or PII leakage.
- Open a private thread with T&S reviewer (include sampled ids + timestamps).
- Check rollout config: slice weights, rollout start time, model variant, fallback mapping, cache warming state.
- Decide within first 15 minutes: resume-with-tweak / hold-and-investigate / rollback.
- Log decision in the rollout decision log (link prepopulated Slack command /rollout-log).

Human review protocol (quick guide):
- Size of review: 50–100 items (mix of flagged and random)
- Mark labels: ok / minor-issue / major-issue / unsafe / not-applicable
- Triage rules: major-issue OR unsafe = treat as regression; 3+ major-issue = immediate rollback
- Document examples with minimal reproducer prompts and anonymized user context for engineering follow-up

Alert templates (Slack)
- Safety alert (short):
  [ALERT] Canary safety spike - canary_id: {{canary}} weight: {{pct}}
  Key signals: safety_flags={{n}}, sample_repo={{link}}
  Immediate action: PAUSE traffic (automated) — @trust-safety @product-oncall please triage.

- Quality alert (short):
  [ALERT] Canary QA delta exceeded - metric: {{metric}} drop: {{abs_delta}}
  Link: {{dashboard}}
  Action requested: steward review + 50-sample human check within 30m.

Roles & responsibilities (practical):
- Steward (first responder): run sample triage, consult T&S / SRE, make binary decision (resume/hold/rollback) and record rationale.
- Product owner: scope experiments and own the hypothesis & rollback criteria pre-committed in experiment brief.
- SRE: validate infra signals, perform mitigations (scale/patch) and revert if system-level cause.
- Trust & Safety: perform safety labelling and sign-off for resume where applicable.

Escalation SLA targets (proposal):
- Safety-critical: 0–5 min page, 15 min human triage, 30 min decision + rollback if confirmed.
- Infra-critical: 5–10 min page, 30 min SRE mitigation window, fallback after 30m if unresolved.
- Quality ambiguous: page within 30m, steward review within 60m, decision logged within 2h.

Example scenario walkthrough (short):
- 11:07 UTC: safety detector fires for canary x (weight 5%). 12 flagged examples in 12m.
- Auto: traffic paused. Slack: posted to #canary-alerts and pages trust-safety.
- Steward (Aisha) pulls samples, finds 9/12 contain sensitive medical advice with hallucinated medication dosing.
- Decision: rollback to baseline, open JIRA-OPS-8743 with sample set. Postmortem requested within 48h.

Edge cases and heuristics:
- Detector tuning drift: if >2 false positives in a week for the same cohort, create a tuning ticket instead of immediate rollback.
- Small cohorts (under 1% traffic): prefer quarantine rather than full rollback if impact localized.
- Flaky telemetry regions: use region-aware baselines (do not compare us-east metrics to ap-southeast baselines).

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Should steward decisions be enforced via a signed-off UI click (audit trail) or via Slack command? tradeoffs: friction vs auditable evidence.
- Need a compact curated review kit (browser extension or one-click console view) for human triage — low priority but high ROI.
- Define standard sample sizes for different traffic levels (50 samples might be enough for 10% weight canary, but not for 1%).
- Add synthetic probe generation for edge-case safety tests during early rollout.

References & links:
- Canary playbook (confluence): CONFLUENCE-Canary-Playbook-2024
- Rollout orchestrator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-orchestrator/pull/412
- Jira ticket template for regressions: JIRA-OPS-REGRESSION-TEMPLATE (link internal)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider adding an escalation matrix graphic to the console (visual decision tree).
- Work with observability to add a "human-review-needed" binary signal to the rollout API.
- Run a table-top with oncall next rotation to validate timings (30m windows feel tight for some QRs).

If you are reading this and want to add a quick example or improve wording, just drop edits inline. This is intentionally terse — we want something a steward can scan in 60s.
